findings.summary: The new input-declaration guard is vacuous for settings.gradle.kts -- the literal it greps for already appears in an unrelated comment at buildSrc/build.gradle.kts:13, so the rootSettings declaration can be deleted whole (comment and all) with the guard still green.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced: delete lines 43-49 of buildSrc/build.gradle.kts (the entire new hunk: the four comment lines plus inputs.file(...settings.gradle.kts).withPropertyName("rootSettings")). `grep -qF -- 'settings.gradle.kts' buildSrc/build.gradle.kts` still matches, because line 13 reads `// ... (see settings.gradle.kts` in this directory ...`. Guard prints nothing and check-harness-tests proceeds. The buildSrc test task then goes UP-TO-DATE across a module rename, RuleListTest/ModulePlanTest/ModuleListDerivationTest never re-run, and the gate reports `ok 61 harness test(s) pass` having executed a cached green -- exactly the W23 defect the guard was written to make unrepresentable, on its fourth occurrence. Fix by anchoring to the declaration rather than the substring (e.g. grep -E '^[[:space:]]*inputs\.file\(.*settings\.gradle\.kts') or, better and one rung lower, by deriving it: run `./gradlew -p buildSrc test`, touch settings.gradle.kts, run again, and assert the task was not UP-TO-DATE.

findings.summary: The CHECK_MODULE_PRINT_RULES door and the rule-count summary both sit BELOW the `no module changed` early exit, so all three RuleListTest cases silently depend on what happens to be in the developer's index. A scripts-only commit -- which does run the harness suite -- turns them red.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced in a scratch clone of the staged tree: stage only `scripts/check-links.sh`. check-harness-tests.sh's delta pathspec includes 'scripts/*.sh', so the buildSrc suite runs. check-module.sh's own delta selection returns MODULES='' and it exits at line 271 with `ok no module changed`. RuleListTest.value() then finds zero `NO_HTTP=` lines and throws `NO_HTTP not printed by the gate`, failing everyModuleNamedByARuleStillExists and theRuleListsDoNotOverlap; theGateAppliesBothRulesToTheRealTree fails its `contains("rule5 applied to 4, rule2 to 2")`. Three red tests, for a commit that changed nothing they constrain. This passes today only because this commit happens to stage buildSrc/build.gradle.kts, a shared-build file that escalates to all eight. The next scripts-only task in the backlog (M0.13, M0.14, M0.19, M0.20) hits it, and the visible pressure will be to weaken the assertion. Fix: set GATE_SCOPE=full in the ProcessBuilder environment of both RuleListTest entry points, or move the rules door above the selection block.

findings.summary: CHECK_MODULE_PRINT_RULES is the only test door that is an environment variable rather than an argv flag, and it exits 0 before the module loop -- an exported value turns the wired hook into a silent no-op.
findings.failure_scenario: `export CHECK_MODULE_PRINT_RULES=1` (a developer debugging RuleListTest, or a stale shell) makes every subsequent `git commit` run check-module.sh, print two NO_HTTP=/NO_CLOUD= lines, call finish and exit 0 -- no Gradle invocation, no rule applied, no `ok` line and no FAIL line. pre-commit renders the hook as Passed. That is a vacuous-pass channel installed into the gate by the very commit that puts it on every developer's commit, and unlike --plan/--select-modules/--check-drift/--list-modules it is reachable from the ambient environment rather than from argv. Fix: make it `--print-rules` alongside the other four doors, which also resolves W27 if the dispatch is placed after the NO_HTTP/NO_CLOUD assignments at line 223.

findings.summary: `rule5 applied to N` claims more than the counter can support: the count proves the branch was entered, not that the rule can still refuse anything.
findings.failure_scenario: Empty HTTP_GROUPS (the mutation the diff's own ModuleGateTest header and backlog row M0.23 admit survives) leaves the summary reading `rule5 applied to 4` while rule 5 matches nothing for any module. An operator reading the success line concludes rule 5 was enforced against four modules; it was tested against four modules with an inert pattern. The counter is worth keeping -- `8 module(s) checked` genuinely is true over skipped rules -- but the wording should say what it measured: `rule5 tested 4 module(s), rule2 2`. Same discipline as scope_note, which deliberately refuses to let a delta pass read like a full one.

findings.summary: The two remaining literals are substring checks over the whole file as well, so the guard states presence-of-text rather than presence-of-declaration.
findings.failure_scenario: Changing `include("*.py", "*.sh")` to `include("*.py") ... exclude("*.sh")`, or moving the fileTree into a comment, satisfies `grep -qF -- '"*.sh"'` while the .sh files stop being declared inputs -- the suite goes UP-TO-DATE across a gate-script edit and prints a cached green. Lower probability than W26 because these literals occur only in the declaration today, but it is the same rung-6 text predicate over a rung-3 derivable fact (gate-design), and the up-to-date-check test named in W26 subsumes all three literals at once.
